problem.claim: Learn diffusion terms and predict diffusion-driven dynamics from observational or real-world data.

gap.claim: Existing approaches use complex bilevel optimization and model only system drift, leaving other diffusion components unmodeled.

contributions.claim: Introduces JKOnet*, a simple model that recovers potential, interaction, and internal-energy components of an underlying diffusion process.
Provides a closed-form optimal solution for linearly parametrized functionals, based on first-order optimality conditions for the JKO scheme.
Reports improved sample efficiency, computational complexity, and accuracy relative to baselines, including cellular-process prediction.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish JKOnet* from existing architectures by combining a simple quadratic-loss objective with recovery of multiple diffusion components rather than drift alone.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that JKOnet* outperforms other baselines in sample efficiency, computational complexity, and accuracy.
On real-world cellular-process data, the authors report state-of-the-art accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost of existing methods.
For linearly parametrized functionals, the authors report a closed-form optimal solution.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diffusion is presented as important for natural processes and generative-model dynamics.
Existing observational-data methods are described as bilevel, complex, and drift-only.
JKOnet* is introduced with a quadratic loss and the ability to recover three diffusion components.
The method is grounded in the JKO energy-minimization view, yields a closed-form solution in a linear case, and is applied to cellular-process prediction.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a modeling simplification—a quadratic loss—to broader component recovery and then reports efficiency and accuracy comparisons.

lessons.interpretation: A compact abstract can make a method claim persuasive by pairing the design choice, the capability it enables, and concrete comparison axes.
lessons.application: When presenting a new method, explicitly connect each architectural or objective-level simplification to the additional quantity it can represent, then report aligned efficiency and accuracy measures.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the claimed capability or comparison is not directly evaluated or theoretically characterized.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset sizes, baseline identities, numerical gains, or evaluation protocols.
The conditions and derivation behind the closed-form solution and the scope of the cellular-process result are not given.
